import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Numerator of $1/\det(M)$ for $M[i,j] = 1/\operatorname{lcm}(i,j)$

Numerator of $1/\det(M)$ where $M$ is the $n \times n$ matrix with
$M[i,j] = 1/\operatorname{lcm}(i,j)$.

*References:*
- [A060841](https://oeis.org/A060841)-/

namespace OeisA60841

/-- The $n \times n$ matrix with entry $(i,j)$ equal to
$1/\operatorname{lcm}(i+1, j+1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. -/
def lcmMatrix (n : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ :=
  Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n ↦ 1 / ((Nat.lcm (i.val + 1) (j.val + 1) : ℚ))

/-- Numerator of $1/\det(M)$ where $M$ is the $n \times n$ matrix with
$M[i,j] = 1/\operatorname{lcm}(i+1,j+1)$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ((lcmMatrix n).det)⁻¹.num

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by
  decide +native

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 4 := by
  decide +native

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 18 := by
  decide +native

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 144 := by
  decide +native

@[category test, AMS 11 15]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 900 := by
  decide +native

/-- The exceptional values of $n$ where $1/\det(M)$ is conjectured to be an integer. -/
def integerDetN : Set ℕ :=
  Set.Icc 1 34 ∪ {36, 38}

/--
"Conjecture: $1/\det(M)$ is an integer only for n: 1 to 34, 36 and 38.
All denominators are powers of two (A000079). - _Robert G. Wilson v_, Aug 02 2015"-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 15]
theorem conjecture :
    (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → (((lcmMatrix n).det)⁻¹.den = 1 ↔ n ∈ integerDetN)) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ k : ℕ, ((lcmMatrix n).det)⁻¹.den = 2 ^ k) := by
  sorry

end OeisA60841

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open], asserting the original conjunction positively.
status_issues.source_status: Disproved. OEIS's Aug 20 2026 comment credits Adamczewski with a counterexample at n = 1807. The cited paper specifically refutes the power-of-two denominator claim; it does not refute the integrality characterization.
status_issues.evidence: https://oeis.org/A060841: “Adamczewski disproves the above conjecture with counterexample for n = 1807, in linked article.” Appendix A of arXiv:2608.11941v2 gives Σ_{k=1}^{1807}(2v₃(k) − v₃(φ(k))) = −1. Since 1/det(M_n) = (n!)²/∏_{k=1}^n φ(k), its reduced denominator at n = 1807 is divisible by 3. I independently confirmed this finite valuation sum in Lean and evaluated the product-formula denominator, whose 3-adic valuation is 1.
status_issues.suggested_change: Mark the combined problem research solved and record its negative resolution, negating the conjunction if retaining a single declaration. Alternatively, split the two claims and record a solved negation of the power-of-two assertion with the n = 1807 counterexample. Do not infer that the integrality characterization itself was disproved.

reformulations.difference: The integrality assertion is expressed as the reduced rational denominator being 1, rather than existence of an integer equal to 1/det(M).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every rational q, q.den = 1 iff there exists z : ℤ with (z : ℚ) = q. In the forward direction take z = q.num, using Rat.den_eq_one_iff; conversely every integer cast has denominator 1. Substituting q = (lcmMatrix n).det⁻¹ and using one_div proves the equivalence for the entire first conjunct, including its quantifiers and exceptional-set condition. This equivalence was proved without using the conjecture in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: All declarations were checked. The matrix correctly indexes 1 through n, and its entries have nonzero LCM denominators. The determinant is positive by the divisor-incidence factorization, giving det(M_n) = ∏φ(k)/(n!)², so rational inverse-at-zero defaults do not affect the claim. The n = 0 extension has determinant 1 and is excluded by both conjecture clauses. Lean directly evaluated the definitions for n = 0..6, confirming all five test theorems. Separate product-formula computations checked the exceptional-range boundaries and the published counterexample; the general determinant-product identity was not reproved in Lean. The final scratch file compiles successfully.
